depth.help: Limit fetching to the specified number of commits from the tip of each remote branch history

dry_run.help: Show what would be done, without making any changes

edit.help: Invoke an editor before committing successful mechanical merge to further edit the auto-generated merge message, so that the user can explain and justify the merge

ff.help: When merging rather than rebasing, specifies how a merge is handled when the merged-in history is already a descendant of the current history

ff_only.help: Only update to the new history if there is no divergent local history

filter.help: Use the partial clone feature and request that the server sends a subset of reachable objects according to a given object filter

force.help: When git fetch is used with <src>:<dst> refspec, it may refuse to update the local branch as discussed in the <refspec> part of the git-fetch(1) documentation

ipv4.help: Use IPv4 addresses only, ignoring IPv6 addresses

ipv6.help: Use IPv6 addresses only, ignoring IPv4 addresses

jobs.help: Parallelize all forms of fetching up to <n> jobs at a time

log.help: In addition to branch names, populate the log message with one-line descriptions from at most <n> actual commits that are being merged

negotiate_only.help: Do not fetch anything from the server, and instead print the ancestors of the provided --negotiation-tip= arguments, which we have in common with the server

negotiation_tip.help: By default, Git will report, to the server, commits reachable from all local refs to find common commits in an attempt to reduce the size of the to-be-received packfile

porcelain.help: Print the output to standard output in an easy-to-parse format for scripts

prefetch.help: Modify the configured refspec to place all refs into the refs/prefetch/ namespace

progress.help: Progress status is reported on the standard error stream by default when it is attached to a terminal, unless -q is specified

prune.help: Before fetching, remove any remote-tracking references that no longer exist on the remote

quiet.help: This is passed to both underlying git-fetch to squelch reporting of during transfer, and underlying git-merge to squelch output during merging

rebase.help: true rebase the current branch on top of the upstream branch after fetching

recurse_submodules.help: This option controls if new commits of populated submodules should be fetched, and if the working trees of active submodules should be updated, too (see git-fetch(1), git-config(1) and gitmodules(5))

refmap.help: When fetching refs listed on the command line, use the specified refspec (can be given more than once) to map the refs to remote-tracking branches, instead of the values of remote.<name>.fetch configuration variables for the remote repository

server_option.help: Transmit the given string to the server when communicating using protocol version 2

set_upstream.help: If the remote is fetched successfully, add upstream (tracking) reference, used by argument-less git-pull(1) and other commands

shallow_exclude.help: Deepen or shorten the history of a shallow repository to exclude commits reachable from a specified remote branch or tag

shallow_since.help: Deepen or shorten the history of a shallow repository to include all reachable commits after <date>

show_forced_updates.help: By default, git checks if a branch is force-updated during fetch

signoff.help: Add a Signed-off-by trailer by the committer at the end of the commit log message

squash.help: Produce the working tree and index state as if a real merge happened (except for the merge information), but do not actually make a commit, move the HEAD, or record $GIT_DIR/MERGE_HEAD (to cause the next git commit command to create a merge commit)

stat.help: Show a diffstat at the end of the merge

strategy.help: Use the given merge strategy; can be supplied more than once to specify them in the order they should be tried

strategy_option.help: Pass merge strategy specific option through to the merge strategy

summary.help: Synonyms to --stat and --no-stat; these are deprecated and will be removed in the future

tags.help: Fetch all tags from the remote (i.e., fetch remote tags refs/tags/* into local tags with the same name), in addition to whatever else would otherwise be fetched

unshallow.help: If the source repository is complete, convert a shallow repository to a complete one, removing all the limitations imposed by shallow repositories

update_shallow.help: By default when fetching from a shallow repository, git fetch refuses refs that require updating .git/shallow

upload_pack.help: When given, and the repository to fetch from is handled by git fetch-pack, --exec=<upload-pack> is passed to the command to specify non-default path for the command run on the other end

verify.help: By default, the pre-merge and commit-msg hooks are run

verify_signatures.help: Verify that the tip commit of the side branch being merged is signed with a valid key, i.e. a key that has a valid uid: in the default trust model, this means the signing key has been signed by a trusted key

b.help: With add, create a new branch named <new-branch> starting at <commit-ish>, and check out <new-branch> into the new worktree

checkout.help: By default, add checks out <commit-ish>, however, --no-checkout can be used to suppress checkout in order to make customizations, such as configuring sparse-checkout

detach.help: With add, detach HEAD in the new worktree

dry_run.help: With prune, do not remove anything; just report what it would remove

expire.help: With prune, only prune missing worktrees if older than <time>

force.help: By default, add refuses to create a new worktree when <commit-ish> is a branch name and is already checked out by another worktree, or if <path> is already assigned to some worktree but is missing (for instance, if <path> was deleted manually)

guess_remote.help: With worktree add <path>, without <commit-ish>, instead of creating a new branch from HEAD, if there exists a tracking branch in exactly one remote matching the basename of <path>, base the new branch on the remote-tracking branch, and mark the remote-tracking branch as "upstream" from the new branch

lock.help: Keep the worktree locked after creation

orphan.help: With add, make the new worktree and index empty, associating the worktree with a new unborn branch named <new-branch>

porcelain.help: With list, output in an easy-to-parse format for scripts

reason.help: With lock or with add --lock, an explanation why the worktree is locked

relative_paths.help: Link worktrees using relative paths or absolute paths (default)

track.help: When creating a new branch, if <commit-ish> is a branch, mark it as "upstream" from the new branch

z.help: Terminate each line with a NUL rather than a newline when --porcelain is specified with list
